stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong will visit China from Wednesday to Saturday, attending the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen before meeting President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang in Beijing — his third visit to China as prime minister.
stories.title: PM Wong to visit China for APEC, meet Xi Jinping and Li Qiang
stories.why: It puts Singapore at the centre of this week's APEC diplomacy, days before the first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin trilateral in Shenzhen.

stories.summary: The US commerce and justice departments confirmed the Justice Department has taken the lead in a criminal investigation of Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed, suspected of diverting restricted Nvidia AI chips to China; they vowed to "bring the full extent of the law" against the company for any criminal conduct.
stories.title: US confirms criminal probe into Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed over Nvidia AI chips
stories.why: The scandal now has a confirmed criminal track — and it is the same case behind the new US chip export controls naming Singapore.

stories.summary: Non-oil domestic exports surged 79.8% year on year in October — the highest since records began in 1976 — driven by ship and boat structures (+S$4.8bn) and pharmaceuticals (+253.1%); exports to the US more than tripled and to China rose 144.9%.
stories.title: Singapore's NODX surges record 79.8% in October, driven by ships and pharma
stories.why: A record export print that shows how much of Singapore's boom rides on AI-linked demand — just as US chip curbs add uncertainty.

stories.summary: The 49th ASEAN Summit closed in Manila with more than 150 outcome documents, and Philippine President Marcos handed the chairmanship gavel to PM Wong; Singapore's 2027 theme is "Deeper Integration, Wider Partnerships".
stories.title: ASEAN Summit ends; Singapore takes the chair for 2027
stories.why: Singapore now chairs ASEAN in its 60th year, with a mandate to deepen integration amid trade fragmentation.

stories.summary: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of US$115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and ahead of the US$109.1 billion consensus, and guided fourth-quarter revenue to US$130 billion; it was the first report since Jensen Huang resigned, and chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate him.
stories.title: Nvidia beats with US$115.8bn revenue in first report since Huang resigned
stories.why: The most-watched earnings of the year delivered — revenue doubled and the outlook beat, steadying the AI trade after days of selling.

stories.summary: Apple, the NSA's classified network, Microsoft Outlook and US air travel were all hit by unrelated outages in recent days, with Apple blaming an internal update and the NSA citing scheduled maintenance; the cluster has fuelled public fears of a cyberattack, which US intelligence denies.
stories.title: Apple joins a parade of technology hiccups in recent days
stories.why: A run of high-profile outages in one week shows how fragile everyday digital services look when they fail together.

stories.summary: At Microsoft Ignite, Satya Nadella launched the AI Transparency Initiative with more than 40 organisations — including Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo — to build open standards for AI transparency, security and governance, plus unique IDs and activity logging for AI agents.
stories.title: Microsoft launches AI Transparency Initiative with 40+ organisations
stories.why: As AI agents act more autonomously, Microsoft is pushing for the audit trail to prove what they did — a governance shift the whole industry will feel.

stories.summary: In closing arguments in the long-running US case against Huawei, prosecutors cast the Chinese tech giant as a villain that stole trade secrets and evaded sanctions, while its lawyers argued the government was criminalising ordinary business competition.
stories.title: In closings, Huawei cast by prosecutors as a villain as its lawyer disagrees
stories.why: The Huawei prosecution has shaped US–China tech policy for years — the closings set up a verdict with wide consequences.

stories.summary: Global stocks fell for a fourth straight session on Tuesday — the Dow down 1.64%, the S&P 500 1.03% and the Nasdaq 0.74% — but sentiment lifted after the close as Nvidia's earnings beat sent its shares up in after-hours trading.
stories.title: Stocks fall, but Nvidia rebound lifts sentiment after earnings beat
stories.why: The sell-off paused on the one report that mattered most — Nvidia's beat is now the market's near-term anchor.

stories.summary: St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said the US economy will likely need "several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027" to bring inflation back to 2%, implying the policy rate could be as much as a percentage point too low; markets now price a December hike at over 95%.
stories.title: Fed's Musalem says several rate hikes likely needed before spring 2027
stories.why: One of the most hawkish Fed voices yet — it reframes the rate path from cuts to hikes, with direct spillover to Asian markets.

stories.summary: China will cut tariffs on about C$400 million of Canadian pork and seafood exports, and Canada will extend tariff exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminium by two years, as Xi Jinping and Mark Carney deepen their January trade reset on the APEC sidelines.
stories.title: China and Canada expand tariff relief after Carney–Xi meeting
stories.why: Another step in the China–Canada thaw — and a template for countries diversifying trade away from the US.

stories.summary: US retail sales rose just 0.2% in October to US$748.2 billion, slowing from 0.8% in September as car sales fell 1.6%; core sales excluding autos rose a stronger 0.6%, and the headline gain sits inside the Census Bureau's margin of error.
stories.title: US retail sales rise just 0.2% in October as big-ticket spending cools
stories.why: The US consumer is cooling on big-ticket items heading into the holidays — a soft read that feeds the Fed's inflation debate.

stories.summary: US jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in what US officials called a self-defence strike, as a third US aircraft carrier entered Middle East waters and the US–Israeli war with Iran settled into a stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.title: US jets strike IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island
stories.why: A live US strike on Iranian soil — the first direct hit on an IRGC missile site in this phase of the war.

stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait bridge for the second time in two days, and the road arch collapsed into the sea, blocking the shipping channel to the Sea of Azov; Zelenskyy said it was a seven-stage operation using Flamingo cruise missiles, Neptune missiles and long-range drones, and Russia opened a terrorism probe.
stories.title: Ukraine's second strike in two days sends Kerch Bridge road arch into the sea
stories.why: Russia's main supply artery to Crimea is now cut indefinitely — a major escalation in the long-range campaign.

stories.summary: A Russian An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo region of Siberia on a scheduled flight, killing all 19 people aboard; the defence ministry cited a preliminary technical malfunction and a commission from the Aerospace Forces is investigating.
stories.title: Russian military transport aircraft crashes in Siberia, killing all 19 aboard
stories.why: A rare fatal crash of a Russian military transport — the second major Russian aviation incident in the war's shadow this week.

stories.summary: Two suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace off Fukuoka for about three minutes each, prompting fighter scrambles and a stern protest from Tokyo; it is the first confirmed Russian airspace violation since September 2024, and the planes then flew between Taiwan and Yonaguni Island.
stories.title: Two suspected Russian aircraft violate Japan's airspace; Tokyo protests
stories.why: A sovereignty breach by Russian military aircraft near Taiwan's airspace — a deliberate signal as regional tensions rise.

stories.summary: Quad leaders met in Manila for the first time in two years, agreeing new critical-minerals deals to cut dependence on any single supplier, a 2027 maritime patrol-aircraft exercise, and a Quad AI accelerator backed by US$85 million for trusted AI ecosystems across the Indo-Pacific.
stories.title: Quad nations agree critical-minerals deals and 2027 patrol-aircraft exercise
stories.why: The Quad's first leaders' meeting of Trump's second term turns the grouping into a supply-chain and maritime-security bloc.

stories.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely's web experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into the sites of 178 organisations — including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, IKEA, Salesforce and Ledger — skimming payment cards, swapping crypto wallet addresses and pushing iOS exploit kits; about US$7,040 in crypto was confirmed stolen before the code was removed.
stories.title: Optimizely supply-chain attack serves malware from 178 major websites
stories.why: One trusted third-party tool turned the world's biggest sites against their own visitors — a textbook supply-chain attack at scale.

stories.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said US intelligence agencies see no sign of a "coordinated cyberattack" or state-sponsored activity behind the week's tech outages, attributing them to simultaneous patching and system upgrades; Senator Mark Warner backed the assessment.
stories.title: US spy chief sees no sign of 'coordinated cyberattack' amid tech outages
stories.why: The top US intelligence official is pushing back on the panic — but the outages themselves show how much strain mass patching puts on systems.

tldr: Singapore: PM Wong heads to China for APEC and meetings with Xi and Li Qiang, as the US confirms a criminal probe into Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed.
Technology: Nvidia beats with US$115.8bn in quarterly revenue in its first report since Jensen Huang resigned.
Finance & global markets: Global stocks fall for a fourth straight session, then Nvidia's rebound lifts sentiment — while a Fed official calls for several rate hikes by spring.
Defence & military developments: US jets strike an IRGC missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island as Ukraine's second strike in two days sends the Kerch Bridge's road arch into the sea.

Information warfare & Information Operations: Hackers hijack Optimizely to serve malware from 178 major websites — as the US spy chief says the week's tech outages show no sign of a coordinated cyberattack.
